prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: tileable diffuse colour texture for a realistic 3D harbour mooring pile in a multiplayer game.
Primary request: a flat, orthographic, photogrammetry-quality surface scan of aged barkless oak timber, historically treated with tar and creosote, weathered for years beside a tidal canal.
Composition: the entire square image is one continuous wood surface, unwrapped and flattened. Fine straight grain runs vertically from bottom to top. It represents approximately 60 cm across and 120 cm along the grain. No plank boundaries, no board joins, no perspective, no background, no rounded-object shading.
Materials: deep muted grey-brown aged wood with narrow silver-grey exposed fibres, fine longitudinal checks, a few restrained irregular splits, slight dark tar residue in grain recesses, scattered small worn knots. Strong convincing fibrous microdetail, low-frequency variation subtle and balanced. Wood grain scale suitable for 30 cm diameter structural piles, not oversized bark.
Lighting: diffuse cross-polarized capture, even neutral illumination edge to edge, colour information only, no cast shadows, highlights or baked ambient occlusion.
Constraints: tile seamlessly on all four edges, vertical grain direction consistent. No text, labels, watermark, hardware, ropes, nails, moss clumps, planks, repeating broad bands, end grain, or dramatic large cracks. Avoid orange new lumber, cartoon texture and exaggerated glossy tar. Opaque image.
